Micchattaniyatattika (The Triplet on Destiny through Wrongness)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.

Dependent on a state fixed in falsehood, a state fixed in falsehood arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate fixed in falsehood, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates.

Dependent on a state fixed in the wrongness (micchattaniyata), a state not fixed (aniyata) arises by way of root condition (hetupaccaya): dependent on aggregates fixed in the wrongness, mind-produced matter (cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa) arises.
Dependent on a state fixed in the wrongness, states both fixed in the wrongness and not fixed arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate fixed in the wrongness, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.

Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one indeterminate aggregate, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter; dependent on two aggregates … dependent on aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
dependent on the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates; dependent on one great primary, there arise three great primaries … [and so forth].
There are two great elements (*mahābhūta*). Dependent on the great elements, there arise mind-produced matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter (*upādārūpa*).

Dependent on states that are either fixed in the wrongness (*micchattaniyata*) or undetermined (*aniyata*), an undetermined state arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on aggregates fixed in the wrongness and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on states that are either fixed in the rightness (*sammattaniyata*) or undetermined, an undetermined state arises by way of the root condition: dependent on aggregates fixed in the rightness and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state fixed in the wrongness (micchattaniyata) by way of object, a state fixed in the wrongness arises by way of object-condition: dependent on one aggregate fixed in the wrongness, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state fixed in the rightness (sammattaniyata) by way of object, a state fixed in the rightness arises by way of object-condition: dependent on one aggregate fixed in the rightness, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….
Dependent on a state of indeterminate nature, a state of indeterminate nature arises by way of object condition:

dependent on one indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates arise. (All conditions)
For this reason, it should be expanded in detail. (Abbreviated.
Pure Section on Enumeration.

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are nine; in object condition (ārammaṇa), three; in predominance condition (adhipati), nine; in proximity condition (anantara), three; in contiguity condition (samanantara), three;

in co-nascence condition (sahajāta), nine; in mutuality condition (aññamañña), three; in support condition (nissaya), nine; in decisive support condition (upanissaya), three; in prenascence condition (purejāta), three; in repetition condition (āsevana), three;

in kamma condition (kamma), nine; in resultant condition (vipāka), one; in nutriment condition (āhāra), nine; in faculty condition (indriya), nine; in jhāna condition (jhāna), nine; in path condition (magga), nine; in association condition (sampayutta) [there are nine].
Three [with root], nine [with dissociation], nine [with presence], three [with absence], three [with disappearance], nine [with non-disappearance]. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive (Anuloma).
1.16.1.2. Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīya)
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra):
Dependent on a state that is not a root and is indeterminate, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root-condition— [namely,] a rootless indeterminate [state].

Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on one great primary … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … in the case of non-percipient beings … the aggregates associated with doubt and associated with restlessness.
Dependent [on these], there arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
By way of non-object condition (*na-ārammaṇa-paccaya*):

Dependent on a state fixed in falsity (*micchattaniyata*), a state that is not fixed (*aniyata*) arises by way of non-object condition—dependent on the aggregates fixed in falsity, mind-originated matter arises. (Abbreviated.)

By way of the non-predominance condition, a state fixed in falsehood arises dependent on a state fixed in falsehood: dependent on aggregates fixed in falsehood, there arises predominance fixed in falsehood.

By way of the non-predominance condition, a state fixed in rightness arises dependent on a state fixed in rightness: dependent on aggregates fixed in rightness, there arises predominance fixed in rightness.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the not-predominance condition:
dependent on one indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … dependent on the aggregates, the [heart-]base arises;
dependent on the base, the aggregates arise; one great primary … non-percipient beings … and so forth.
Dependent on a state fixed in the wrongness immediately following [it], a state of indeterminate result arises by way of non-immediate condition. (Abbreviated; all conditions should be expanded.
Section on Enumeration.
Pure: one by way of not-root; five by way of not-object; three by way of not-predominance; five by way of not-proximity; five by way of not-contiguity;
five by way of not-mutuality; five by way of not-strong-dependence; six by way of not-prenascence; nine by way of not-postnascence.

In the case of "not-by-repetition," there are five; in the case of "not-by-kamma," three; in the case of "not-by-resultant," nine; in the case of "not-by-nutriment," one; in the case of "not-by-faculty," one;
in the case of "not-by-jhāna," one; in the case of "not-by-path," one; in the case of "not-by-association," five; in the case of "not-by-dissociation," two; in the case of "not-by-absence," five;
in the case of "not-by-disappearance," five. (Thus it should be counted.)

1.16.3. Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra)
1.16.3.1. Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Root Condition (Hetu)
Conditioned by a state fixed in the wrong way (micchattaniyata), a state fixed in the wrong way arises by way of root condition … three.
Conditioned by a state fixed in the right way (sammattaniyata), a state fixed in the right way arises by way of root condition … three.
Conditioned by an undetermined state (aniyata), an undetermined state arises by way of root condition: conditioned by one undetermined aggregate … [and so on].

Conditioned by [one] aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … conditioned by the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates; conditioned by one great primary … conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the indeterminate aggregates.

Conditioned by a state that is undetermined (aniyata), a state determined for falsehood (micchattaniyata) arises by way of root condition (hetupaccaya): conditioned by the [heart-]base, aggregates determined for falsehood arise.

Conditioned by a state that is undetermined, a state determined for rightness (sammattaniyata) arises by way of root condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, aggregates determined for rightness arise.

Conditioned by a state that is undetermined, states both determined for falsehood and undetermined arise by way of root condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, aggregates determined for falsehood arise; conditioned by the great elements (mahābhūta), mind-originated matter (cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa) arises.

Conditioned by a state that is undetermined (*aniyata*), states that are both determined toward rightness (*sammattaniyata*) and undetermined arise by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): conditioned by the [heart-]base, the aggregates determined toward rightness arise; conditioned by the great elements, mind-originated matter arises.

Conditioned by a state that is both determined toward wrongness (*micchattaniyata*) and undetermined, a state determined toward wrongness arises by way of root-condition: conditioned by one aggregate determined toward wrongness and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] …

Conditioned by states that are both fixed in the wrongness and unfixed, an unfixed state arises by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates fixed in the wrongness and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises.
Conditioned by states that are both fixed in the wrongness and unfixed, states that are both fixed in the wrongness and unfixed arise by way of root condition:
conditioned by one aggregate fixed in the wrongness and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise.
... pe ... two aggregates ... pe ... conditioned by aggregates certain to wrongness and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises.
Conditioned by states certain to rightness and indeterminate states, a state certain to rightness arises by way of root condition. (Three questions; similar to those on wrongness.
Object, etc.

Conditioned by a state fixed in falsehood, a state fixed in falsehood arises by way of object-condition … (abbreviated; to be analyzed as in the section on conditions in the Wholesome Triplet) … by way of non-disappearance condition.
Numerical Section:
Pure.

In the case of root condition, there are seventeen; in object condition, seven; in predominance condition, seventeen; in proximity condition, seven; in contiguity condition, seven; in co-nascence condition, seventeen;
in mutuality condition, seven; in dependence condition, seventeen; in strong-dependence condition, seven; in prenascence condition, seven; in repetition condition, seven;
in kamma condition, seventeen; in resultant condition, one; in nutriment condition, seventeen; in faculty condition...

Seventeen [factors] in the jhāna, seventeen in the path, seven in association, seventeen in dissociation, seventeen in presence, seven in absence, seven in disappearance, and seventeen in non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive (Anuloma).

1.16.3.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra) Conditioned by an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the not-root condition (nahetupaccaya): [namely,] a rootless indeterminate [state].

Conditioned by one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base; conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates.
Conditioned by one great primary …pe… in the case of non-percipient beings …pe… conditioned by the eye-base, there arises eye-consciousness …pe… conditioned by the body-base …pe…
Conditioned by [the heart-base], body-consciousness arises. Conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless indeterminate aggregates arise.
Conditioned by both the aggregates associated with doubt and the restlessness associated with doubt, as well as the base, delusion associated with doubt and restlessness arises.
(Not-object condition)

Conditioned by a state fixed in the wrongness, a state not fixed arises by way of non-object condition: conditioned by aggregates fixed in the wrongness, mind-produced matter arises. (This is similar to the Wholesome Triplet; five [answers] should be made. Non-predominance:

Conditioned by a state fixed in the wrongness, a state fixed in the wrongness arises by way of non-predominance condition: conditioned by aggregates fixed in the wrongness, predominance fixed in the wrongness arises.

Conditioned by a state fixed in the rightness of perfection (*sammattaniyata*), a state fixed in the rightness of perfection arises by way of the not-predominance condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*): conditioned by aggregates fixed in the rightness of perfection, there arises predominance fixed in the rightness of perfection.
Conditioned by an undetermined state (*aniyata*), an undetermined state arises by way of the not-predominance condition:

conditioned by one undetermined aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … [etc. … conditioned by two aggregates … [etc. … at the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi-kkhaṇe*).
...pe... for non-percipient beings ...pe... conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises ...pe...
conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises. Conditioned by the [heart-]base, the indeterminate aggregates arise.
Conditioned by an indeterminate state, a state fixed in falsehood arises by way of the not-predominance condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, the predominance fixed in falsehood arises.

Conditioned by a state of the undetermined class, a state of the fixed-in-rightness class arises by way of the non-predominance condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, the predominance that is fixed-in-rightness [arises].

Conditioned by a state that is both fixed-in-wrongness and undetermined, a state of the fixed-in-wrongness class arises by way of the non-predominance condition: conditioned by the aggregates fixed-in-wrongness and the [heart-]base, the predominance that is fixed-in-wrongness [arises].

Conditioned by a state that is either fixed in the rightness [of the path] (*sammattaniyata*) or unfixed (*aniyata*), a state fixed in the rightness arises by way of the not-predominance condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*): conditioned by aggregates fixed in the rightness and the [heart-]base, the predominance [state] fixed in the rightness arises.
Not-immediate, etc.:

conditioned by a state fixed in the wrongness (*micchattaniyata*), an unfixed state arises by way of the not-immediate condition …pe… by way of the not-absence condition … by way of the not-disappearance condition.
In the Enumeration Chapter, under the Pure [Dependent] Section:
one by way of not-root condition, five by way of not-object condition, seven by way of not-predominance condition, five by way of not-proximity condition, and five by way of not-contiguity condition.
Five [conditions] do not condition by way of mutuality; five do not condition by way of strong-dependence; six do not condition by way of prenascence;

seventeen do not condition by way of postnascence; five do not condition by way of repetition; seven do not condition by way of kamma; seventeen do not condition by way of result; one does not condition by way of nutriment;

one does not condition by way of faculty, jhāna, or path; five do not condition by way of association; two do not condition by way of dissociation; five do not condition by way of absence; five do not condition by way of disappearance. (It should be counted in this manner.)
The Negative. 1.16.3.3.
Positive-Negative Conditionality.
The Root-Dyad.
With root condition, there are five [instances] not being object; seven not being predominance; five not being proximity;
five not being contiguity, not being mutuality, and not being strong-dependence; six not being prenascence; seventeen not being postnascence;
five not being repetition; seven not being kamma; seventeen not being result; five not being association; two not being dissociation; [and five] not being absence.
Five [are] in the non-disappeared; five [are] in the non-disappeared. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive-Negative. 1.16.3.4. Negative-Positive Condition.
Non-cause dyad:
With non-cause condition, one [count] for object, one for proximity (*anantara*)—[abbreviated]—one for non-disappearance (*avigata*). (It should be counted in this manner.
This is the positive-negative sequence.
The Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra).
1.16.4. The Section on Support (Nissayavāra).
The Section on Support is similar to the Section on Conditions.
1.16.5. Chapter on Association (Saṃsaṭṭhavāra) 1.16.5.1.
Positive Order of Conditions: Section on Analysis (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra)

Conditioned by the root-cause, a state fixed in falsehood arises in association with a state fixed in falsehood: three aggregates associated with one aggregate fixed in falsehood … pe … two aggregates … pe ….

Conditioned by the root-cause, a state fixed in rightness arises in association with a state fixed in rightness: three aggregates associated with one aggregate fixed in rightness … pe … two aggregates … pe ….

In association with a state of indeterminate destiny, a state of indeterminate destiny arises by way of root condition: in association with one aggregate of indeterminate destiny, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … and so forth.
Object Condition, etc.:
In association with a state fixed in falsehood, a state fixed in falsehood arises by way of object condition … up to … non-disappearance condition.
In the Enumeration Chapter, under the Pure Condition:
three for root, three for object …pe… three for kamma, one for result, three for nutriment …pe… three for non-disappearance. (It should be counted in this manner.)
Positive Order.
1.16.5.2. Analysis Section on the Negative Order of Conditions.

An indeterminate state arises in association with an indeterminate state by way of the not-root condition: three aggregates associated with one rootless indeterminate aggregate … two aggregates … and so on … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … and so on.
Not-predominance:

A state fixed in the wrongness arises in association with a state fixed in the wrongness by way of the not-predominance condition: a predominance fixed in the wrongness associated with aggregates fixed in the wrongness.

A state fixed in rightness arises in association with a state fixed in rightness by way of the not-predominance condition: the predominance fixed in rightness associated with the aggregates fixed in rightness.

An indeterminate state arises in association with an indeterminate state by way of the not-predominance condition: three aggregates associated with one indeterminate aggregate … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … and so forth.
[The section on] not-precedence and so forth.

A state fixed in rightness arises in association with a state fixed in rightness by way of not-prenascence condition: in the formless plane, three aggregates associated with one aggregate fixed in rightness … two aggregates … [and so on] … A state of no fixed destiny arises in association with a state of no fixed destiny by way of not-prenascence condition:
in the formless plane, three aggregates associated with one aggregate of no fixed destiny … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on] …
A state fixed in falsehood, being conjoined with a state fixed in falsehood, arises not by way of postnascence condition. (Complete.
Not-by-repetition, etc.:

A state that is undetermined, being conjoined with a state that is undetermined, arises not by way of repetition condition—three aggregates conjoined with one undetermined aggregate … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … and so forth.
A state fixed in falsehood arises in association with a state fixed in falsehood by way of neither-kamma-condition nor-resultant-condition. (Abbreviated.

A state of the undetermined class arises in association with a state of the undetermined class by way of neither-jhāna-condition—namely, the fivefold sense-consciousness …pe… by way of neither-path-condition—namely, rootless undetermined states …pe….

A state fixed in rightness arises in association with a state fixed in rightness by way of the non-dissociation condition: in the formless realm, three aggregates associated with one aggregate fixed in rightness …pe… [two aggregates …pe…].

A state of no fixed destiny arises in association with a state of no fixed destiny by way of the non-dissociation condition: in the formless realm, three aggregates associated with one aggregate of no fixed destiny …pe… [two aggregates …pe…].
Section on Enumeration.

With the pure [condition], there is one by way of not-root, three by way of not-predominance, two by way of not-prenascence, three by way of not-postnascence, one by way of not-repetition, three by way of not-kamma, three by way of not-resultant, one by way of not-jhāna, one by way of not-path, and two by way of not-dissociation. A state fixed in the wrongness (micchattaniyata) is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state both fixed in the wrongness and not fixed (aniyata).
A state fixed in the rightness (sammattaniyata) is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition... and by way of decisive support condition, for a state fixed in the rightness.
A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state not fixed by way of object-condition, conascence-condition, decisive-support-condition, and postnascence-condition.
A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state both fixed in rightness and not fixed by way of conascence-condition.
A state not fixed is a condition for a state not fixed by way of object-condition and conascence-condition.

Conditioned by way of object-condition … by way of decisive-support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of postnascence condition … by way of kamma-condition … by way of nutriment-condition … by way of faculty-condition.
An indefinite state is a condition for a state fixed in the wrongness [of views] by way of object-condition … by way of decisive-support condition … by way of prenascence condition.
An indefinite state is a condition for a state that is fixed in the rightness [of liberation] by way of decisive support condition and by way of prenascence condition.
Both states that are fixed in the wrongness [of bondage] and those that are indefinite are conditions for a state that is fixed in the wrongness by way of conascence and prenascence.
Both states that are fixed in the wrongness and those that are indefinite are conditions for an indefinite state by way of conascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty.
States that are fixed in the rightness [of liberation] and states that are unfixed are related to a state fixed in the rightness by way of conascence and prenascence.
States that are fixed in the rightness and states that are unfixed are related to an unfixed state by way of conascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty.
1.16.7.2. Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīya)

In the Enumeration Chapter, regarding the Pure [conditioning], there are thirteen [factors] excluding the root condition; there are thirteen excluding the object, the predominance, the contiguity, and the immediate conditions; and [thirteen] excluding the co-nascence condition.
With not-root, nine; with not-mutuality, nine; with not-dependence, nine; with not-strong-dependence, thirteen;
with not-prenascence, eleven; with not-postnascence, thirteen; with not-repetition, thirteen; with not-kamma, not-resultant, and not-nutriment, thirteen … pe … with not-path, thirteen;
with not-association, nine; with not-dissociation, seven; with not-presence, seven; with not-absence, thirteen.
Thirteen [factors] are not yet arisen; seven are not unarisen. (Thus it should be counted.
The Negative. 1.16.7.3.
Positive-Negative Conditionality.
Hetuduka: With root condition, there are seven [instances] for non-object, seven for non-predominance, seven for non-proximity, seven for non-contiguity,
three for non-mutuality, seven for non-strong-dependence … pe … seven for non-path, and three for non-association.
With non-dissociation, three; with non-absence, seven; with non-disappearance, seven. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive-Negative. 1.16.7.4. Negative-Positive Conditionality.

In the "Not-root" dyad: with the not-root condition, there are five [modes] in the object condition, eight in the predominance condition, five in the proximity condition, five in the contiguity condition,

nine in the conascence condition, three in the mutuality condition, thirteen in the support condition, seven in the decisive support condition, three in the prenascence condition, and [three] in the postnascence condition.
Three in repetition; three in repetition; seven in kamma; one in resultant; seven in nutriment;
seven in faculty, jhāna, and path; three in association; five in dissociation; thirteen in presence; five in absence;
five in disappearance; thirteen in non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.)
The Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
The Triplet on Destiny through Wrongness (Micchattaniyatattika) is finished.
